key_points: Long-term ACE-inhibitor therapy can benefit patients with heart failure or left-ventricular dysfunction.
ACE inhibitors and angiotensin receptor blockers are effective in chronic stable coronary disease and can reduce mortality in patients with myocardial infarction.
Studies suggest renin-angiotensin system inhibitors may lower cardiovascular events in patients with stable coronary artery disease.
Colchicine may be beneficial for secondary prevention of cardiovascular disease.
It is considered for use in patients with chronic coronary disease.
Influenza vaccination is associated with a reduction in cardiovascular events in high-risk patients.
Regular immunizations are recommended for preventing adverse cardiovascular outcomes.
